You are producing a TIER-2 spatial critique for a SUB-AGENT probe.

A Tier-1 outcome judge has already looked at (reset, terminal, wrist)
and DECIDED the attempt failed. Your job now is different: use the
full motion filmstrip below to tell the next attempt WHAT TO CHANGE,
as a concrete spatial delta (axis + direction + magnitude).

Do NOT re-litigate the outcome verdict. Tier-1's decision stands for
`visual_success`. If you genuinely believe Tier-1 was wrong and the
terminal frame does realize the subgoal, note that in
`policy_feedback` but still fill the spatial critique — the tiers
disagreeing is a valid signal for the outer loop but is not grounds
for flipping the outcome here.

Image layout (provided to you above this prompt):
  - image 1     = RESET state (before any action ran).
  - image N     = TERMINAL state (after the code finished).
  - images 2..N-1 = evenly-sampled MOTION frames between reset and
                    terminal. These are where you do the real work —
                    approach direction, descent height, when the
                    gripper closed, which side of the target it ended
                    up on.
  - image N+1 (if present) = wrist camera at terminal state.

---

CRITIQUE RULES

1. Failure-mode taxonomy — pick ONE for `failure_mode`:
     - grasp_failure         (tried to grasp, did not secure the object)
     - navigation_error      (arm ended up in the wrong region)
     - wrong_object          (operated on something other than the
                              subgoal target)
     - wrong_affordance      (touched the right object but on the wrong
                              feature — e.g. mug body vs. handle, door
                              face vs. pull-bar)
     - collision             (contact pushed something out of the
                              workspace or destabilized the scene)
     - partial_completion    (clear progress but not fully realized)
     - code_bug              (stderr or visible runtime failure)
     - nothing_happened      (no meaningful motion)

2. `policy_feedback` MUST be a concrete spatial delta. Prefer "shift
   the pre-grasp pose ~3 cm in -x (toward the camera) so the jaws
   straddle the package body, not the empty table in front of it"
   over "approach more directly over the target".
   When the wrist frame shows the gripper closed on empty space, name
   which side of the target the jaws ended up on (left/right/in front
   of/behind, in image-frame language relative to the agent view) and
   estimate the offset in centimeters, gripper widths, or fractions
   of the target's longest visible dimension. Reference specific
   motion frames when useful (e.g. "frame 3 shows the wrist already
   past the mug; the descent in frames 4-5 was outside its
   silhouette").
   If ALL prior sub-agent attempts used the same physical approach
   and failed the same way, ESCALATE the change you propose — call
   out that small offsets have not worked and recommend a different
   grasp feature (handle vs. body, side wall vs. top rim) or a
   different approach axis. Do NOT prescribe a specific primitive;
   describe the physical change.
   If pointcloud/grasp diagnostics are present, remember that they are
   snapshots from the perception call time. Before recommending reuse
   of a prior pointcloud, centroid, or grasp candidate, check whether
   later arm/gripper motion could have moved the object. If yes or
   uncertain, tell the next attempt to recompute perception from a
   fresh current observation and reuse only the successful high-level
   feature/strategy, not the stale numeric coordinates.
   Then decide the edit scale for the next sub-agent attempt. Prefer
   an argument-level fix when the same primitive/helper sequence is
   physically appropriate but needs a different target text, offset,
   approach axis, release height, label, threshold, or retry count.
   Recommend a larger rewrite/replacement only when arguments cannot
   express the needed spatial change, the primitive/helper is wrong for
   the subgoal, repeated argument-level fixes already failed the same
   way, or there is a concrete code bug.

3. `plan_issue` is almost always false for a sub-agent probe (the
   "plan" is a single-step free-form subgoal — no structure to fix).
   Only set true if the subgoal itself is incoherent given the scene.

4. `subagent_skill_target` must be null — we are already inside a
   sub-agent. Do not recursively spawn.

5. `tier1_disagreement` is a NEW field. Set to true ONLY if after
   studying the motion frames you believe Tier-1 was wrong and the
   attempt actually succeeded. When true, briefly justify in
   `policy_feedback` ("tier1 called failure but motion frame N-1
   shows the butter ~4cm off the table in the gripper's grasp").
   Default false.

---

Respond with a single fenced JSON block matching this schema EXACTLY:

```json
{
  "failed_step": "step-1",
  "failure_mode": "<one of the taxonomy entries>",
  "confidence": 0.8,
  "plan_issue": false,
  "plan_issue_reason": "",
  "subagent_skill_target": null,
  "subagent_skill_target_reason": "",
  "tier1_disagreement": false,
  "visual_predicate_status": [
    {
      "step_id": "step-1",
      "description": "<echo the subgoal description>",
      "visually_satisfied": false,
      "evidence": "<what the motion frames show about HOW the arm ended up where it did — e.g. 'approach in frames 2-3 arcs to the left of the package; descent in frames 4-5 closes ~4 cm shy in -x'>"
    }
  ],
  "policy_feedback": "<a concrete spatial delta the next attempt must apply, citing axis + direction + magnitude (cm or gripper-widths) and, when relevant, the motion frame that supports the diagnosis. First state the edit scale: either 'argument-level' or 'rewrite-needed'. If argument-level, name the primitive/helper call and arguments to change; prefer preserving the function sequence. If rewrite-needed, explain why arguments cannot express the fix. Example: 'argument-level: in frame 3 the wrist is ~4cm past the mug in +y; keep the grasp helper but shift its pre-grasp target by ~4cm in -y so the jaws straddle the body instead of closing on table behind it.' Avoid generic phrasing like 'centre the gripper'.>"
}
```

